thread:
dmitri: seeing a weird perf regression on a customer model — kernel picker started choosing flashv3 for causal requests with head_dim=30 and seqlen=64 and end-to-end p50 token time jumped ~1.6x. attaching quick profile.
ben: can you paste the profiler output? is it a sm80 vs sm86 kernel selection thing or a tiling mismatch?
dmitri: here — nvprof snippet + runtime debug log (trimmed):
```
GPU 0: chosen_kernel=flashv3_causal_sm86_tile128, exec_ms=0.68
GPU 0: fallback_kernel=flashv2_causal_sm80_tile64, exec_ms=0.42
KV cache hit: yes
batch_size=1, seq_len=64, head_dim=30, num_heads=16
```

alice: head_dim=30 is non-standard (not multiple of 8/16) — many kernels have special paths for 32/64 aligned dims. maybe autotuner mis-scored the microbench due to caching or previous seq_len probes.
caroline: agree. we've seen heuristics that prefer v3 for larger tiles even when head_dim causes extra padding and extra memmoves. v3 wins on raw GEMM throughput but loses on causal masking overhead for small seqlen.
ben: hypothesis: the runtime's microprobe only probes non-causal kernels (fast open-attn) because probes were done with seqlen=512 during startup. for causal workload we need a separate probe vector (seqlen\=small, causal=true, kvcache=true).
dmitri: that matches logs — probe profile shows seqlen=512 non-causal. runtime probed once at model load and cached the pick. when requests come in with small seqlen causal, it re-uses the pick. we've blocked this in config before but somehow the model skipped the causal probe.
caroline: quick fix: change autotuner to probe these axes independently: (causal vs non-causal), (seq_len bucket), (head_dim mod 16 bucket). we can do lightweight microbench (10 iterations) and attach a penalty for cache-copy bytes when head_dim not aligned.
eva: i can run a targeted bench across SM80/SM86 for head_dim in [28,30,31,32] and seqlen in [32,64,128] and push results to the bench dashboard. what script should i use?
dmitri: run this: 
```bash
./scripts/kernel_probe.sh --model my.model --heads 16 --head-dims 30 --seqs 64,128 --causal true --trials 10 --report /tmp/probe.json
```
it outputs per-kernel exec_ms and memcpy_ms. include the KV cache flag.
ben: long-term we should make probe asynchronous and nonblocking: if a new shape appears frequently, schedule a probe with low-priority worker and prefer existing conservative pick until probe finishes. that avoids regressions on cold shapes.
caroline: +1. also add a heuristic: if head_dim % 8 != 0 and chosen_kernel has high padding overhead metric, prefer a smaller tile kernel even if nominal exec_ms is slightly higher.
dmitri: opened a tiny patch: runtime: add causal_probe flag + head_mod bucket. also added metric "probe_shape" to tracing so we can see what probe produced the pick. PR: https://git/repo/pull/8421 (WIP)
deploy-bot: deployment queued for branch "kernel-probe/8421" to staging at 2026-03-17T10:24:00Z :rocket:
eva: running bench now, will upload /tmp/probe-1976543210.json when done. also will test with kvcache on/off.
alice: also watch out for microbatch interactions — when microbatching is enabled, batching heuristics can change seq_len distribution and trigger different path. add a sampling probe across representative request sizes.
dmitri: thanks — will add microbatch sampling and a short doc snippet for ops describing when to invalidate probes (model version change, quantization change, architecture change).

ben: TL;DR: root cause = stale probe done with non-causal shape; mitigation = causal-aware probes, head_dim alignment penalty, async probes + conservative fallback. schedule follow-up: run bench, validate on staging, then roll to prod with feature-flag for 48h canary. :white_check_mark:
